events/1321_ravenna/phases/0/transitionT:
The church of Santo Stefano. Twice as many candles lit as usual.
Boccaccio opens the last volume of his notes.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/0/announcemen: Boccaccio: “The story has reached its end. A city by the sea took him in — Ravenna. You are about to see how a man who had lost everything finished writing everything.”
events/1321_ravenna/phases/1/narrative: Around 1318 the lord of Ravenna, Guido Novello da Polenta, sends messengers to invite him. The sea pines rustle, his children come to join him — the last stop of the exile, and it feels like a home.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/1/instruction: Walk between the pines and the court. Meet the people here.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/1/npcs/0/dial: That you would come is Ravenna's good fortune, master. The house is ready and the pay is generous — no. Not a retainer. A master.
I write verse too. Some day… would you look at mine and correct it? (The lord bows like a pupil.)
events/1321_ravenna/phases/1/npcs/1/dial: Father. I have taken vows at the convent of Santo Stefano here in the city.
My name in religion is — Sister Beatrice.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/1/npcs/2/dial: Copies of the Inferno and the Purgatorio are passing from city to city. Master — the Paradiso is still a few cantos short.
Finish it. All Italy is waiting.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/2/narrative: The church of Sant'Apollinare. Gold mosaics from the sixth century, burning for eight hundred years.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/2/instruction: Click the things in the church that move him.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/2/npcs/0/dial: The gold tiles flicker on and off in the candlelight, like a sea of light gone solid. The saints stand in a gold that never ends.
A gold vault… so the light of Heaven has been seen on earth after all.
(The whirlpools of light, the rose of light, the river of light in the Paradiso — the first sketch of all of it is on a ceiling in Ravenna.)
events/1321_ravenna/phases/2/npcs/1/dial: A letter comes from Giovanni del Virgilio, a scholar in Bologna: “What a waste, to write a lasting work in the common tongue. Write it again in Latin, and I will get you the laurel crown in Bologna.”
(He picks up his pen and sends back two country poems in Latin verse — faultless craft, and the answer is one word: no.)
The girl in the bakery cannot read Latin. The common tongue is thirteen cantos away from winning.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/3/transitionT:
Summer 1321. Ravenna and Venice fall into a quarrel.
Dante goes to Venice as Guido's envoy to settle it, and comes back through the marsh channels —
mosquitoes, fever. Malaria.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/3/announcemen: Dante Alighieri dies in Ravenna, fifty-six years old. His children are at the bedside. The last thirteen cantos of the Paradiso — they search the whole study, and no one finds them.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/3/dufu_reacti:
Bread will not fail me anywhere…
Only the Paradiso… thirteen cantos short.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/4/narrative: Eight months later. A story people still tell —
events/1321_ravenna/phases/4/panels/0/di: His son Jacopo sees his father in a dream. White robe, smiling, light all around him.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/4/panels/1/di: “What you are looking for,” his father lifts a hand and points at the wall of his old bedroom, “is there.”
events/1321_ravenna/phases/4/panels/2/di: They pull back the wall hanging — there is a small niche in the wall, and inside it a damp, mouldy stack of manuscript.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/4/panels/3/di: They brush off the mould. The writing can still be read — the last thirteen cantos of the Paradiso.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/4/panels/4/di:
l'amor che move il sole e l'altre stelle —
It is love that moves the sun and the stars.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/rule: Dante's universe: the earth in the middle, nine heavens wrapped around it. The further out, the faster it turns — because it is closer to God.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/0/h: People who could not keep a vow
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/0/n: Piccarda is here. Her own brother dragged her out of the convent and forced her to marry — someone else broke the vow for her, and still she can go no higher than the lowest ring. She says: here I am content.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/1/h: People who did good, and wanted the credit too
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/1/n: The emperor Justinian is here, speaking up for Roman law. Mix a little wish for fame into your good deeds and you cannot climb higher than this.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/2/n: Their love went over the line while they lived. They are still loving now, only this time it points the right way. Dante did not put anyone lower just for loving too easily.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/3/n: Twelve wise souls turn in a ring, Thomas Aquinas among them. The interesting part: here Aquinas speaks well of a rival he argued with all his life.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/4/h: People who fought for their faith
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/4/n: The souls line up into a huge cross. Cacciaguida comes down off the cross to claim Dante as his own descendant — and it is here that he says that line about how salty another man's bread is.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/5/n: The souls spell out a line of writing first, then turn into an eagle. The eagle can talk, and what it says is “we” — justice is not one person's business.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/6/n: A golden ladder climbs from here, and you cannot see the top. This ring is oddly quiet — Dante says that any higher up, Beatrice can no longer smile at him. The smile would burn him.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/7/h: The three apostles' test: faith, hope, love
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/7/n: St Peter tests faith, St James hope, St John love. That examination down on earth he never passed. This one he answers all the way through.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/8/h: The ring that turns all the rest
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/spheres/8/n: Nothing solid here, only nine ranks of angels turning around one very bright point. Time for the whole universe starts moving from this ring.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/finale/line: You set out from a dark wood.
Through Hell, up the mountain of Purgatory, and on into the stars.
Not one person you met on the way came out of nowhere —
every one of them was somebody Dante knew in Florence.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/5/finale/coda:
The last line of the whole poem reads:
It is love that moves the sun and the other stars.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/6/transitionT: Boccaccio closes his notes. The church is very quiet.
events/1321_ravenna/phases/6/announcemen: Echoes down the years · The end

Boccaccio: “That is a legend. But the Paradiso really is complete — and that is the miracle itself. Today, in 1373, Florence pays me to lecture on Dante; Ravenna still refuses to hand back his bones. He said it himself: bread will not fail me anywhere. Rest, poet. And this Comedy of his — let us who come after add one word to it without asking: Divine (Divina).”
events/1321_ravenna/phases/6/dufu_reacti: It is love that moves the sun and the stars.
quiz/1321_ravenna/quizzes/0/question: In Paradiso XXIV–XXVI, what do the three apostles each test Dante on?
quiz/1321_ravenna/quizzes/0/explanation: St Peter tests faith, St James hope, St John love. Dante passes them all, and Peter circles him three times like a ring of light — set against the rigged exam Du Fu sat in 747, where nobody passed. This examination is fair.
quiz/1321_ravenna/quizzes/1/options/0: Florence — beside the San Giovanni Baptistery
quiz/1321_ravenna/quizzes/1/explanation: On the night of 13 September 1321 Dante died of fever in Ravenna and was buried there. Florence asked for the bones again and again; Ravenna still will not give them back. The city that once ordered him burned, and then wanted him back, keeps only an empty tomb.
quiz/1321_ravenna/quizzes/2/question:
The last line of the Divine Comedy:
“It is love that moves the sun and the ___”
quiz/1321_ravenna/quizzes/2/explanation: “l'amor che move il sole e l'altre stelle” — it is love that moves the sun and the stars. All three parts, the Inferno, the Purgatorio and the Paradiso, end on the same word: stars (stelle).
